claims.text: Subprocess transport for explicitly configured, non-interactive agent CLIs.
claims.why: The class SubprocessAdapter is designed to run configured CLIs as subprocesses, and the profiles are for non-interactive, one-shot invocations.

claims.text: This is a process/event normalization layer, not a universal agent protocol
claims.why: The adapter normalizes subprocess output into AgentEvents, but requires verified command profiles and parsers per CLI.

claims.text: Built-in profiles are limited to CLIs whose local --help contract is exercised by tests and whose execution is one-shot.
claims.why: The chunk does not include tests or --help contract verification; cannot confirm claim.

claims.text: Antigravity isn't listed: no ``agy`` executable or stable JSON protocol exists on this machine, and a desktop/IDE session does not imply a callable CLI contract.
claims.why: Claim references external environment ('this machine') and non-existent executable; cannot verify from code alone.

claims.text: These profiles describe one-shot, non-interactive invocations.
claims.why: Both profiles have streaming=True, close_stdin_after_prompt=True, and no resume support, consistent with one-shot.

observations.what: claude profile includes --verbose and --input-format text flags that are not standard for the official Claude CLI (which uses --input-format json). May cause startup failure.
codex profile uses 'exec' subcommand and --sandbox flag; may not match actual Codex CLI interface.

create_session: when prompt_mode is 'stdin' and stdin_prompt_marker is None, the prompt is not added to command args and not sent to stdin. The code only sends prompt to stdin if stdin_prompt_marker is set (line: 'cmd.append(self._config.stdin_prompt_marker)'). But later it checks 'if prompt and self._config.prompt_mode == "stdin":' to send prompt to stdin. This means if stdin_prompt_marker is None, prompt is not sent to stdin either (because the condition uses prompt and prompt_mode, but the earlier branch for stdin with marker sets cmd, but does not send prompt to stdin in that branch). Actually, the code: if prompt and prompt_mode == 'stdin' and stdin_prompt_marker: add marker to cmd. Then later if prompt and prompt_mode == 'stdin': send prompt to stdin. So if stdin_prompt_marker is set, prompt goes to stdin; if not, prompt is not sent to stdin. This may be intentional but is unclear.
_Session.stderr_task reads stderr into bytes but the result is never used or awaited. If stderr output is large, the task may accumulate memory indefinitely.
events method is a stub returning an empty async iterator; the adapter cannot stream events until it is implemented.
close_stdin_after_prompt defaults True, which closes stdin immediately after writing the prompt. For streaming runtimes that expect to read further input, this will break the session.
